violation_type.title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation (26 TAC §747.2703(4)(D))
violation_type.short_title: Positive Methods of Discipline and Guidance - Brief Supervised Separation
violation_type.typical_finding: An assistant caregiver placed a crying child in time out in a play yard for 6 minutes. The primary caregiver then moved the play yard with the child inside of it to a bedroom. The child was alone in the bedroom with the door shut for 9 minutes. This was observed through video obtained during the investigation.

finding_variants.text: An assistant caregiver placed a crying child in time out in a play yard for 6 minutes. The primary caregiver then moved the play yard with the child inside of it to a bedroom. The child was alone in the bedroom with the door shut for 9 minutes. This was observed through video obtained during the investigation.

A child that has been biting other children was put in a seperate area. There was two baby gates seperating him from the main play area. The provider indicated that this seperation to prevent him from biting.
Primary caregiver was asked how long are the children placed in  timeout and she stated for five minutes for children younger than five years old.
Toddler children and children up to 4 years old are being required to remain in time out for up to 5 minutes which over the one minute per year requirement.
Based on the information obtained during the course of the investigation, children under the age of 5yo were placed in time-out for 5-10 minutes.

A child in care was separated in a different room at the operation due to behavioral issues, however he was separated for over an hour while I was present.     This was corrected when the child was removed from timeout and allowed to go back with the other children in care.
